title: Land Bank of the Philippines v. Court of Appeals
summary: The Supreme Court ruled that the determination of just compensation in agrarian reform cases is a judicial function. Courts are not bound by the formula prescribed by the Department of Agrarian Reform, though they must consider the factors enumerated in Section 17 of RA 6657.
doctrine: The determination of just compensation is a judicial function which cannot be limited by legislation or administrative regulation. While courts must consider the DAR formula, they are not bound by it. Just compensation must be the full and fair equivalent of the property taken from the owner.
fullText:
PANGANIBAN, J.:

The core issue is the proper determination of just compensation for lands acquired under the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program.

The determination of just compensation is a judicial function. The executive department or the legislature may make the initial determination, but when a party claims a violation of the guarantee against the taking without just compensation, no statute, decree, or executive order can mandate that its own determination shall prevail over the court's findings.

Section 17 of RA 6657 enumerates the factors to be considered in determining just compensation. While the courts should be guided by these factors, the ultimate determination of what constitutes just and fair compensation rests with the judiciary.
